title: A single-line shift block shows three text lines: customer name, unit number, and the line name
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A single-line shift exists on the grid (VIN toggle off).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Read the shift block's text lines from top to bottom.
expected: 1. Line 1: the customer name.
2. Line 2: the unit number.
3. Last line: the name of the scheduled line.
4. No work order number appears on the block.

title: Whole-order and multi-line-subset shifts both read 'N Lines' on the block - the detail modal spells out the exact scope
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Schedule: Edit to set up (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Two shifts exist for a 4-line work order: one whole-order shift (4 lines) and one 2-line subset shift.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Read the last text line of the whole-order shift's block.
2. Read the last text line of the subset shift's block.
3. Open each shift's detail modal.
expected: 1. The whole-order block reads '4 Lines'.
2. The subset block reads '2 Lines' - the block does not distinguish whole-order from subset beyond the count.
3. Each detail modal lists exactly which lines the shift covers.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: Multi-line/whole-order block reads 'N Lines' pinned by the Claude design (§3, block shows lineName|'N Lines'); confirm live. Driver: Claude design §3.

title: VIN appears as an extra block line only when the VIN toggle is on, in day and week views only (month omits it)
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A shift exists for a unit that has a VIN.
3. You are on the Schedule page; the VIN toggle in 'Filter and Display' is OFF.
steps: 1. In week view, read the shift block (VIN off).
2. Turn the VIN toggle ON in 'Filter and Display'.
3. Read the block again in week view, then in day view, then in month view.
expected: 1. VIN off: the block shows three lines, no VIN.
2. VIN on: a VIN line is added to the block in week view and day view.
3. Month view still omits the VIN line even with the toggle on (space constraints).
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.

title: Shift blocks default to blue; a custom colour can be set per shift
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Schedule: Edit to set up (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Two shifts from the SAME work order exist (for example on different technicians), plus one shift from a different work order whose color has been changed.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Look at a newly created shift block's colour.
2. Open the shift detail modal and set a custom colour via the colour picker.
3. Compare that shift with another shift from the same work order.
expected: 1. By default every shift block is blue (the default shift colour).
2. A custom colour can be assigned per shift via the colour picker in the detail modal.
3. Colour is per shift - it is NOT tied to the work order, so two shifts from the same order do not automatically share a colour.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: V1 rule (Jira SV-8690, latest-wins over the older requirements.md §10): all shift blocks default to blue; custom colours are optional per shift (NOT tied to the work order). SCH-COLOR-01 already agrees. Driver: SV-8690 §4.4, §10. Verify live at VIU.

title: The conflict icon is the only icon on a shift block - no work order number and no scope icons
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Schedule: Edit to set up (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.

steps: 1. Inspect the unconflicted block for icons and a work order number.
2. Inspect the conflicted block.
expected: 1. The unconflicted block shows NO icons and NO work order number - only its text lines.

title: Shifts whose times do not overlap share a single lane - the row keeps its normal height

steps: 1. Look at the technician's row on that day.
expected: 1. Both shifts sit in the same single lane, one after the other.

title: Visible lanes cap at 3 - additional overlapping shifts collapse into a '+N more' affordance that opens a popover
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Schedule: Edit to set up (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.

steps: 1. Count the visible lanes in the technician's row.
2. Find and click the '+N more' affordance.
expected: 1. At most 3 lanes are visible.

title: Lane stacking and the '+N more' overflow apply in day, week, and month views
permissions_required: Schedule: View to observe; Schedule: Edit to set up (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. One technician has several overlapping shifts on the same day (from SCH-LANE-03's setup).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. View the day in day view and note the stacking/overflow.
2. Switch to week view and look at the same day's cell.
3. Switch to month view and look at the same day.
expected: 1. All three views handle the overlap without blocks visually colliding.
2. Week and month views reach the '+N more' overflow sooner than day view (their cells are narrower), but the same cap-and-overflow model applies.
3. The overflow affordance opens the hidden-shifts popover in each view.

title: A technician can hold multiple shifts on the same day from different work orders

expected: 1. Both shifts are created and shown on the same day for the same technician - multiple same-day shifts are allowed.

title: Day view auto-scrolls on load and day navigation so the working-day start sits at the left edge (with a small buffer)
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Technicians have configured start times; note the EARLIEST one (or the business-hours start / 7:00 AM if none).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Switch to day view and look at where the timeline is scrolled to.
2. Navigate to the next day with the toolbar arrow and look again.
expected: 1. On load and on each day navigation, the timeline is auto-scrolled so the working-day start sits at the left edge of the visible area, with a small buffer (roughly 30 to 60 minutes) before it.
2. The start used is the earliest technician's configured start; if no tech hours are set, business hours; otherwise 7:00 AM - so no shifts sit off-screen to the left.
3. The timeline is not stuck there - it remains a full 24-hour scrollable timeline.
design_ref: Claude design (authoritative, Branko Q0): build/schedule/spec-v1-2026-07-22/design-notes-claude.md (prototype Schedule.dc.html). spec_1 added the Design link to the doc.
notes: The 30-60 minute buffer is spec-approximate - confirm the actual buffer live.

title: Manual scrolling is not overridden - auto-scroll fires only on load or day navigation

3. Then navigate to the next day.
expected: 1. Your manual scroll position stays put - nothing jumps you back to the morning while you remain on the same day.
2. Scrolling works across the entire 24-hour timeline (midnight to midnight).

title: Dragging a shift horizontally moves its start time, snapping to 15-minute intervals
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit (spec §14.1 - horizontal drag is an Edit interaction).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift exists on a technician's day-view timeline.
3. You are on the Schedule page in day view.
steps: 1. Drag the shift block horizontally along the timeline and release at a position between clean quarter-hours.
2. Open the shift and read its new start time.
3. Undo via the toast if needed and restore the original time.
expected: 1. The shift moves along the timeline as you drag.
2. The released start time snaps to a 15-minute interval (for example 9:15, 9:30 - never 9:22).
3. The duration is unchanged by a horizontal move.
4. A toast with Undo appears for the move.

steps: 1. Drag the shift's RIGHT edge further right and release.
2. Drag the shift's LEFT edge and release.
3. Open the shift and read its times.
expected: 1. Dragging the right edge extends/shortens the end time (start unchanged).

4. The shift's duration on the grid matches the modal's start/end.
